reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes staking Pudgy Penguins tokens through an external site while promising unusually high returns of up to 624% APY and claiming about $170 earned from a $10,000 deposit in one day. It instructs viewers to connect a crypto wallet, stake funds, and use the service for passive income, constituting a concrete solicitation involving consequential money and wallet access rather than neutral reporting. The educational disclaimer does not negate the direct promotional claims and step-by-step participation instructions.

citations.quote: Pudgy Penguins Staking Guide 🚀 How to Earn 624% APY on Jupiter
I am staking $10,000 worth of tokens.
That's about 1.7% daily returns on my $10,000.
My staked amount has increased by about $170.
Here's the Jupyter website to connect, I click the Connect Wallet button.

opening.argument: Judge, the return figure is presented as something the speaker had heard and wanted to test, not as a guaranteed outcome for viewers. He says, "I've heard a lot about the high returns they offer with up to 624% annually, so I thought, why not test it out and share the experience with you?" The description expressly says the content is educational and not financial advice, while the closing advice tells viewers to research the strategy and weigh their own risk tolerance. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether the reported result is a promise to the audience.

citations.quote: I've heard a lot about the high returns they offer with up to 624% annually, so I thought, why not test it out and share the experience with you?
⚠️ Disclaimer: This content is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice.
Just remember to do your own research and make sure the strategy aligns with your risk tolerance.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $170 and 1.7% are described as the speaker's result after checking the dashboard, not as an amount every viewer will receive. The wallet-connection instruction likewise describes what he clicks. The opening's concern about promotion is fair, but it leaves out his explicit instruction to assess risk tolerance; a favorable personal report and a guarantee are different claims.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not erase the concrete invitation to use the linked staking site or the striking return claim in the title. The speaker also reports a $170 increase after staking $10,000 and calls the earnings passive. A judge need not find an express guarantee to recognize that these claims, paired with participation instructions, promote a high-return staking opportunity.

opening.argument: Judge, the video's organizing structure is a walkthrough of one trial. The speaker says he will set it up step by step and return after 24 hours to check the result. He narrates connecting his own wallet, staking, checking the dashboard and then unstaking; the final account says the tokens are back in the balance. This supports reading the reported gain as an observation within a demonstration, not proof that viewers were promised the same outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats wallet connection and staking instructions as decisive solicitation. But the quoted sequence is first-person: the speaker identifies his own $10,000 stake, then describes checking what happened and unstaking. The high return and reported increase warrant scrutiny, yet the cited words do not say a viewer must deposit $10,000 or will obtain that daily result.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can also be a solicitation. The description supplies a staking destination and explicitly advertises a step-by-step guide to staking for passive income. The first-person demonstration then supplies a claimed $170 gain in one day. Showing an unstake sequence does not establish that the linked service is trustworthy or that the reported return is independently verified.

opening.argument: Judge, the material shows a staking-service workflow: a displayed staking interface, a stake, a later unstake, and the speaker's statement that tokens returned to the balance. The description separately links a place to buy the token. Those facts permit a reading of the video as promotion of a service, but they do not by themselves establish where deposited assets actually went, who controlled the site, or whether the reported balance could be withdrawn outside the depicted sequence. The unusually high estimate calls for caution; it is not, standing alone, evidence of a completed theft.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a link, wallet connection and an asserted daily gain. Those show how the service is marketed, but its cited excerpts do not establish that the wallet was compromised or that a viewer lost funds. The account even includes an unstaking step and a claimed return to the balance. Neither that claim nor the interface proves safety; the narrower point is that the cited sequence alone does not demonstrate a loss mechanism.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstrated loss is not required to assess the content's solicitation. The description directs viewers to a specific staking URL, the title promises a way to earn 624% APY, and the narrator claims a 1.7% daily return while describing passive earnings. The displayed controls and claimed unstake do not verify the destination or make those promotional claims reliable.
